HomePage.hero_description: Sem-P (semaglutide) is a once-weekly injectable medication for adults with type 2 diabetes or with overweight/obesity requiring medical management.
HomePage.hero_description_two: It works by reducing appetite, slowing gastric emptying, and improving the body’s insulin response. This leads to improved blood sugar control and sustained weight loss.
HomePage.hero_list_description1: It lower blood sugar when used with healthy eating and exercise
HomePage.hero_list_description2: It reduces the risk of serious heart problem like heart attack or stroke in people who already have heart disease
HomePage.hero_footer_description: Sem-P comes in easy-to-use pens and vials, so you and your doctor can choose what works best for you.
HomePage.semp_three_ways: Landmark clinical trials demonstrate Sem-P significantly reduces major adverse cardiac events in adults with Type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease - beyond weight loss alone.
HomePage.first_way: 26% Reduction in Major Adverse CV Events risk for cardiovascular patients<sup>[1]</sup>
HomePage.third_way: Lowers risk of heart attack, stroke, and cardiovascular mortality
HomePage.semp_once: Why choose between quality and convenience? Access focused care through telehealth or in-person appointments, designed to suit your schedule.
HomePage.semp_first_desc: ​How weight and metabolism affect your health
HomePage.semp_second_desc: Type 2 diabetes happens when the body does not use insulin properly. This causes high blood sugar, which can harm the heart, kidneys, and blood vessels.
HomePage.semp_third_desc: GLP-1 treatments are medicines that help the body control blood sugar naturally, protect organs, and support weight loss with once-a-week injections.
HomePage.semp_fourth_desc: Obesity is a medical condition, not a willpower problem. It is affected by metabolism, appetite, and genetics. It often occurs along with diabetes and heart disease.

HomePage.storage_text: Store Sem-P Pen in the refrigerator (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze. Do not use if Sem-P has been frozen. Keep the Pen in its original carton to protect from light. Keep Sem-P out of the reach of children.
HomePage.answer_one: Sem-P is administered once weekly via subcutaneous injection in the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm. The vial and Pre-filled pen is designed for self-administration and includes built-in safety features. Rotate injection sites each week to minimize irritation. Your Health Care Provider (HCP) will demonstrate proper technique during your first appointment.
HomePage.answer_two: Like all medications, GLP-1 treatments can cause side effects. The most common are mild nausea, vomiting,  abdominal pain, and decreased appetite which typically improve after the first few weeks. Your Health Care Provider (HCP) will discuss all potential side effects and monitor your progress to ensure treatment is safe and effective.
HomePage.answer_three: Treatment begins with Sem-P 0.25mg weekly for 4 weeks to minimize side effects. Dosage is gradually increased (0.5mg, 1mg, up to 2mg) based on your tolerance and weight loss response. Your Health Care Provider (HCP)  will adjust your dose every 4 weeks until reaching your optimal therapeutic level. Never adjust dosing without medical guidance.
HomePage.answer_four: Sem-P is contraindicated in patients with personal/family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2. Not recommended during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or for patients with severe gastroparesis. Discuss your complete medical history with your Health Care Provider (HCP) to ensure Sem-P is safe for you.
HomePage.question_five: Can I use Sem-P if I have pre-diabetes with obesity?
HomePage.answer_five: Yes, Sem-P may be used for people with prediabetes and obesity to help with weight loss and improve blood sugar control. It works by helping your body use insulin better and reducing appetite. Your doctor will decide if it’s right for you based on your health, weight goals, and blood sugar levels.
